turns.patient_response: Hello, Dr. Smith. I keep getting stuck redoing the same checks and routines over and over at work, even when I know they’re unnecessary, and it’s starting to derail my projects and my life. It's reached a point where I just can't seem to break the cycle on my own.

turns.patient_response: It is definitely to prevent a specific bad outcome; I get looping thoughts that if I miss a tiny detail like a wrong bolt size, a part will fail and people will get hurt. To prevent that, I end up opening the same CAD files or emails ten times in a row to recheck them. Even though I know the fear is irrational, I just can't seem to stop.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes having 'looping thoughts' about missing a tiny detail that will cause a part to fail and hurt people, which represents intrusive and unwanted obsessions.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient reports opening CAD files or emails ten times in a row to recheck them to prevent a bad outcome, which represents repetitive checking compulsions.

turns.patient_response: Yes, I do. I get these vivid, looping mental images of parts failing and people getting hurt because of a tiny detail I might have missed, like a minor tolerance error.
